source: Cassini RSS Rev7E X-band + UVIS beta Cen x6 (visible tau)
quantity: normal optical depth, geometric / visible-equivalent (extinction efficiency 1)
notes: Shape: RSS_2005_123_X43_E (Marouf, CO-SR-RSS-4/5-OCC-V2.0, 2018), 1 km resolution, 0.25 km sampling, ring elevation -23.57 deg, radii + pole/timing corrections. Radio tau is an extinction tau (Q_ext = 2 for particles >> 3.6 cm): measured tau_X/tau_UVIS = 2.00 in the C ring and Cassini Division; RSS is rescaled by a 50 km smooth ratio map R = <tau_UVIS>/<tau_X/2> (R ~1.0 C ring, ~1.15 ramps, ~1.3-1.9 A ring, wake/geometry effects). B ring 92150-117020 km (RSS saturated): mean TRANSMISSION of 6 UVIS HSP beta Cen occultations (Colwell et al., CO-SR-UVIS-HSP-2/4-OCC-V3.0), B = 66.7 deg, 1 km bins, registered to the RSS radius scale (offsets < 0.35 km); tau = -mu ln<T>; 2849 samples (712 km, 2.9% of the B ring) are detection-limited (<T> < 2 sigma photon noise, i.e. tau > ~8) and are set to 8 (opaque). Low-elevation views of the real A/B rings are more transparent than a homogeneous slab with this tau (self-gravity wakes): RSS at B = 23.6 deg sees ~25-45% lower normal tau in the A ring and ~40% lower in B1. Eccentric features (Titan, Maxwell, Huygens ringlets; B-ring outer edge m=2; A-ring outer edge m=7) and density-wave phases are a snapshot at the RSS Rev7E longitude (2005-123). Gap floors smoothed (+-1.5 km), negative noise clipped; gap edges deconvolved to steps at the half-level crossing (data resolution ~1 km; real edges are sharp at tens of m). NaN = no data: r < 74300 km (D ring, tau ~1e-3 below detection) and r > 136774 km (Roche Division / F ring).
